en.title: Microsoft Ditches Sales Data Firm Circana Amidst Declining Console Figures
en.summary: Microsoft has stopped sharing its digital sales data with analytics group Circana, a move that follows reports of an 18% drop in Xbox console sales. This decision raises questions about transparency in the gaming industry.
en.body:
In a move that may further cloud the already murky waters of the video game industry's sales landscape, **Microsoft** has reportedly ceased sharing its digital sales figures with **Circana**, a leading US analytics firm. This revelation comes directly from **Mat Piscatella**, an executive at Circana, who confirmed the change on the social platform Bluesky. Piscatella stated that **Microsoft** is "no longer a digital panel participating publisher," offering little further detail on the specific reasons behind this abrupt decision.

This development arrives hot on the heels of Circana's July 2026 report, which highlighted a concerning 18 percent year-over-year decline in **Xbox** console sales. While other console manufacturers also experienced sales drops, **Microsoft**'s withdrawal from data sharing suggests a potential unwillingness to have its performance scrutinized so publicly, especially when that performance is trending downwards. This decision has immediate implications for how the market perceives the success of **Microsoft**'s gaming division and its flagship franchises.

## The Impact on Transparency

For years, data from firms like Circana has served as a crucial, albeit sometimes imperfect, barometer for the health of the gaming market. Publishers like **Microsoft** traditionally participate in these panels, providing raw sales data that analysts then use to compile comprehensive reports. When a major player like **Microsoft** opts out, the accuracy and completeness of these reports are inevitably compromised. **Circana** will now have to rely on estimations and projections for **Microsoft**'s sales, a process that can be particularly challenging given the consistent chart-topping performance of **Microsoft**-owned titles, most notably the **Call of Duty** franchise. The lack of direct data means that the true market share and dominance of **Microsoft**'s gaming ecosystem will become increasingly opaque to both industry observers and, importantly, its own passionate fanbase.

## Fan Reaction and Industry Concerns

The gaming community thrives on understanding trends, celebrating successes, and analyzing the competitive landscape. When sales data becomes less transparent, it can foster speculation and distrust. Fans often look to these reports to gauge the popularity of their favorite platforms and games, influencing purchasing decisions and discussions within the community. The decision by **Microsoft** to withhold data, particularly after a period of reported sales decline, could lead to increased fan anxiety and frustration. It raises questions about whether other major publishers might follow suit, further fragmenting the available market intelligence and making it harder for anyone to get a clear picture of where the industry truly stands. The reliance on estimations means that the perceived success of titles like **Call of Duty** could be inflated or deflated without concrete evidence, leaving enthusiasts in the dark.

## What's Next

With **Microsoft** no longer providing direct digital sales figures, **Circana** will continue to provide its monthly reports based on estimations and available data from other sources. The industry will be watching closely to see if this trend of reduced data sharing continues and how it ultimately impacts the perception and analysis of the global gaming market.

content_raw: As gaming consoles and digital sales continue to decline and meander for big publishers, some of them are opting to not share their numbers with analysts. Now, Microsoft joins those and will no longer give Circana, a leading US analytics group, its digital sales figures. This was confirmed by Circana’s Mat Piscatella on Bluesky. Piscatella didn’t provide too many details about what might have prompted Microsoft to make such a decision and merely said that “Microsoft is no longer a digital panel participating publisher.” Microsoft is no longer a digital panel participating publisher. — Mat Piscatella (@matpiscatella.bsky.social) 2026-08-20T13:39:56.868Z This comes just a couple of days after Piscatella published Circana’s July 2026 figures that indicated an 18 percent decline in sales of Xbox consoles compared to the same month last year. Other consoles saw similar drops, or even more significant ones, but it seems Microsoft isn’t so happy about its poor performance being publicly known. Circana will now have to estimate Microsoft sales for every report, and since a lot of its games, including the Call of Duty franchise, usually top charts every single month, especially in the United States, then we’re going to have a real problem. Estimates and guesses are about in the same category no matter how well-informed they may be, and we’ll not have a clear picture of how dominant CoD and Microsoft really are, if at all. As shown in Circana’s latest sales post, every single one of the estimated top 10 games is based on projections and analysis rather than raw data points, and with Microsoft now out of the picture, things are going to be even muddier.
